_: The technique catalogue: what we know how to install, when it is worth
installing, and what happened the times we did.
Three rules make this a recommender rather than an opinion:
1. `appliesWhen` is executable against a project fingerprint. A technique with
no machine-checkable condition is not a technique, it is a preference, and
the validator refuses it.
2. `prevents` names one concrete failure. If nobody can name the incident the
technique would have stopped, it does not belong here — that test alone
removes most of what gets adopted for looking modern.
3. There is no `ring` field. Adopt / trial / assess / hold is DERIVED from the
evidence below, so the catalogue cannot claim confidence it has not earned.
Thoughtworks moves its rings on a whiteboard twice a year; ours move when a
measurement comes back.
Verdicts:
worked        applied, and a measurement afterwards showed the effect
no-effect     applied, and the measurement showed nothing
rejected      proposed, client declined — kept, because five refusals in a
row say the technique is badly argued or too expensive
gap-observed  its ABSENCE was measured causing a problem; evidence for the
technique, but not yet evidence that we delivered it
Where an external standard exists we borrow it. Arguing with our own ten-point
scale is easy; arguing with `14 pairs fail WCAG AA` is not.

conventions-gate.name: Conventions ratchet
conventions-gate.what: Hold new code to the conventions measured in this repository, with today's violations accepted as debt.
conventions-gate.prevents: A codebase drifting into two ways of doing everything, which is what happens to every repository where the rule is written down and nothing checks it.

cost.ongoing: none; it runs in the existing gate

conventions-gate.enforcedBy: scripts/gate/conventions.mjs on edit, commit and CI
conventions-gate.standard: none — the conventions are the project's own

evidence.outcome: Green on install across 89 files; caught 4 violations across 4 dimensions on a probe file; the pre-commit hook blocked the commit.
Its own AGENTS.md requires the `@/` alias; measured at 54%. The rule was written and unchecked.
Styling split three ways (49/36/15), export style 76/25, props 78/22 — no check on any of them.

agent-contract.name: Generated agent contract
agent-contract.what: An AGENTS.md written from the repository's own measured conventions, with a CLAUDE.md pointer beside it.
agent-contract.prevents: Every agent on the project inventing its own house style, and a hand-written contract going stale the first time the team changes its mind.
agent-contract.enforcedBy: regeneration; the file is an artifact, never hand-edited
agent-contract.standard: AGENTS.md — read natively by Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Zed

evidence.outcome: .ds/CONVENTIONS.md generated: 6 enforced, 3 leaning, 1 left to the team.

component-registry.name: Machine-readable component registry
component-registry.what: Every component, its props, its closed unions and one line saying what it is for, generated from source and read on demand.
component-registry.prevents: An agent inventing a component or a prop that does not exist — the most frequent measured failure in agent-written UI.
component-registry.enforcedBy: gen-registry --check plus a verify step on written code

evidence.outcome: 82 components, 219 tokens, 7 blocks; index generated so it cannot go stale.
127 components, 853 props, 407 union values extracted from shipped types in seconds.

judgment-tier.name: Written judgment: descriptions, twins, vocabulary
judgment-tier.what: One sentence per component saying when to reach for it instead of its neighbour, the confusable pairs settled in writing, and one meaning per shared prop name.
judgment-tier.prevents: Choosing the wrong component — which compiles, passes review and is still wrong. A props registry does not catch it.

cost.install: a day per library, reusable across every client on that stack

judgment-tier.enforcedBy: profile validation refuses a component with no description

evidence.outcome: Of 127 components, exactly 1 ships a usable description in its types. The line that decides which component gets picked is the one no library provides.
120 descriptions, 12 twin pairs and 4 vocabulary entries authored; profile passed validation.

judgment-tier.deliveredBy: authored by a person into bindings/<profile>.json — about a day per library, and reusable across every client on that stack

token-tiers.name: Three-tier tokens
token-tiers.what: Settings feed primitives feed semantic roles; product code addresses the role tier only.
token-tiers.prevents: Values decided outside the system: a literal does not survive a rebrand and takes no part in theming.

cost.install: days on an existing codebase; extraction first, then invert the direction

token-tiers.standard: Design Tokens Community Group format for the export

evidence.outcome: 95% of colour values and 100% of sizing from tokens — the one dimension with a check on it.
97% colour, 100% sizing. Same result, same reason.

token-export-dtcg.name: DTCG token export
token-export-dtcg.what: Tokens published in the Design Tokens Community Group format, generated from source and round-trip checked.
token-export-dtcg.prevents: A system that can be copied but not consumed: CSS custom properties are invisible to Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio and any path back into Figma.

cost.ongoing: generated with a --check in the gate

token-export-dtcg.enforcedBy: tokens --check: every alias resolves, every value survives a round trip

evidence.outcome: 219 tokens exported; three independent counts agreed.

screen-specs.name: Spec before screen
screen-specs.what: A new screen starts as a machine-checkable spec validated against the component registry.
screen-specs.prevents: Agreeing to a screen that cannot be built. Arguing about a zone costs a minute; arguing about a built screen costs an afternoon.

cost.ongoing: a spec per new screen, which replaces the ticket rather than adding to it

evidence.outcome: One spec checked against two libraries: buildable on the first-party system, and on MUI it surfaced two decisions (no page header component; Avatar has no size prop) before any code was written.

screen-specs.deliveredBy: one file per agreed screen, written by `ds draft` when a requirement arrives — there is nothing to install on day one

golden-examples.name: Executable golden examples
golden-examples.what: One real module per component that compiles, renders and passes axe — not a snippet in a document.
golden-examples.prevents: Documentation drifting from the component. The example is what an agent copies, so it lies exactly when a prop gets renamed.

cost.install: the expensive part of adopting a foreign library

golden-examples.enforcedBy: the test suite renders every example; the registry publishes them

evidence.outcome: Every component ships one; tsc breaks when a prop is renamed.

gate-graph.name: Gate as a dependency graph with modes
gate-graph.what: One list of gates with declared dependencies, from which edit / commit / CI modes are derived, run in parallel with bounded workers.
gate-graph.prevents: Two hand-maintained `&&` chains drifting apart, which they always do — a check present locally and missing in CI is the normal end state.
gate-graph.enforcedBy: the runner itself; modes cannot lose a gate the graph declares

evidence.outcome: check is 28 steps, check:ci is 20. Eight checks never reach CI, including the three custom linters that encode what no off-the-shelf tool knows — while AGENTS.md states the difference is only the machine-specific visual baselines.

gate-self-tests.name: Tests for the checks themselves
gate-self-tests.what: Every custom linter has a test proving it fails on bad input.
gate-self-tests.prevents: A rule silently stopping working. The gate stays green and nobody finds out.

evidence.outcome: 60 tests on components, none on the six custom linters that hold the project-specific rules.

contrast-check.name: Contrast resolved from tokens
contrast-check.what: Colour pairs checked in every theme, computed from the token files rather than from hand-mirrored hex; accepted misses record their ratio and may not get worse.
contrast-check.prevents: Shipping unreadable text in one theme, found by a user rather than by the build.

a11y-tests.name: Accessibility assertions on rendered output
a11y-tests.what: Every golden example rendered and checked with axe; every stateful component carrying a keyboard and ARIA test.
a11y-tests.prevents: Accessibility checked by eye, which is accessibility not checked.

visual-baselines.name: Visual baselines
visual-baselines.what: Every golden example screenshotted in a real browser, in every theme, against committed images.
visual-baselines.prevents: Layout regressions no assertion sees; this is the only check that looks at the rendered result.

cost.ongoing: review of every accepted image; baselines are machine-specific

visual-baselines.enforcedBy: a visual gate outside CI where baselines differ per machine

evidence.outcome: no CI runner with a browser, and nobody would review the images
no browser in their CI yet
no browser runner in this repo yet
no browser runner here

context-budget.name: Token budget on agent-read files
context-budget.what: A ceiling, in tokens, on the files every agent reads on every task, with the full registry held to a per-entry ceiling instead of being must-read.
context-budget.prevents: A contract that does not fit in context, which is a contract that is not followed.
context-budget.enforcedBy: a context gate that fails when the ceiling is passed

evidence.outcome: A MUI registry runs to 127 components and 853 props. On a large library the budget matters more, not less.

mcp-surface.name: Registry over MCP
mcp-surface.what: The registry's answers served to any agent, including agents not working in this repository.
mcp-surface.prevents: The contract being reachable only by whoever cloned the repo, so everyone else guesses.

agent-evals.name: Evals on agent output
agent-evals.what: A reference and a set of breaks, generated from this repository's own exemplar and its enforced conventions, so the gate can be asked whether it would notice an agent violating them.
agent-evals.prevents: A gate nobody has tried to slip past. Every convention it claims to enforce is claimed until something breaks it and gets caught.
agent-evals.enforcedBy: node evals/run.mjs — a surviving break exits non-zero

secret-scan.name: Secret scanning on what git carries
secret-scan.what: A scan over the tree git actually holds, not just the working copy.
secret-scan.prevents: A credential reaching a remote, after which rotation is the only remedy.
secret-scan.standard: OpenSSF Scorecard treats this as a baseline practice

ci-pipeline.name: The same gate graph in CI
ci-pipeline.what: CI runs a mode of the same graph the hook runs, so the two cannot disagree.
ci-pipeline.prevents: A gate that only exists on the machine of whoever remembered to run it.
ci-pipeline.standard: DORA — continuous integration is one of its measured capabilities

evidence.outcome: No CI configuration at all; the entire gate depends on each clone having run one git config command.
Same.

dead-code-check.name: Dead code and unused exports
dead-code-check.what: Unreferenced files, exports and dependencies reported as a triage list.
dead-code-check.prevents: A codebase where nobody can tell what is load-bearing, which makes every refactor a gamble.

cost.ongoing: triage; it is a tool, not a gate

dead-code-check.enforcedBy: knip, run outside the blocking gate

duplication-check.name: Cross-file duplication detection
duplication-check.what: Copy-paste detection across the source with a threshold in the gate.
duplication-check.prevents: The same component built twice, after which both drift and neither is authoritative.

promotion-scout.name: Promotion on second use
promotion-scout.what: A check that finds what has been built twice across packages and should move into the shared system.
promotion-scout.prevents: A shared system failing quietly: everyone builds what they need locally, the gate stays green, and the system stops being where components live.

cost.ongoing: a reason and a reopening condition per finding

promotion-scout.enforcedBy: a scout step in the gate

dead-token-sweep.name: Dead token sweep
dead-token-sweep.what: Remove tokens that are declared and never referenced, and keep them out with a check.
dead-token-sweep.prevents: A palette nobody trusts: when a third of the tokens are unused, nobody can tell which ones are the system and which are leftovers, so people stop reading the file and hardcode instead.
dead-token-sweep.enforcedBy: a dead-token check beside the token generator

evidence.outcome: 19 tokens declared and never referenced in the system's own styles.
19 dead tokens carried into the app through the vendored copy.

architecture-rules.name: Executable architecture rules
architecture-rules.what: Module boundaries expressed as dependency-cruiser rules that fail the build, rather than as a diagram nobody runs.
architecture-rules.prevents: A cycle or a forbidden edge arriving unnoticed. Measured on one repository, a hand-written traversal saw 90 modules where a configured cruise sees 257 and finds the cycle.

cost.ongoing: a rule per boundary the team decides

evidence.outcome: A real circular import between src/data/salim.ts and src/data/salimMockData.ts, invisible to a traversal that cannot resolve aliases.

edit-hook.name: Lint on every edit, before it lands
edit-hook.what: A PostToolUse hook runs the gate on each file an agent writes and blocks the edit on failure.
edit-hook.prevents: An agent producing twenty files and discovering at the end that the first one broke a rule. Feedback that arrives after the work is feedback that costs the work.
edit-hook.standard: Claude Code hooks: deterministic scripts at defined lifecycle points

evidence.outcome: An edit hook plus a Stop gate is why this repository's conventions hold at 100% where unchecked dimensions sit at 54%.

stop-gate.name: A turn cannot finish while the build is red
stop-gate.what: A Stop hook refuses to end an agent's turn while the gate fails.
stop-gate.prevents: An agent declaring a task done on top of a failing build, which is the single most common way agent work has to be redone.

evidence.outcome: Present here and absent in every app, which is where the drift is.

pretooluse-guard.name: A checkpoint before a tool runs
pretooluse-guard.what: A PreToolUse hook inspects what an agent is about to do and can refuse it.
pretooluse-guard.prevents: A destructive or out-of-scope command executing and being discovered afterwards. This is the only hook that runs before the action rather than after.

cost.ongoing: a rule per class of command refused

pretooluse-guard.standard: Claude Code hooks — PreToolUse is the primary security checkpoint

crosstool-contract.name: One contract every agent can read
crosstool-contract.what: Rules live in AGENTS.md, the cross-tool name, with a four-line CLAUDE.md importing it so Claude Code reads the same text.
crosstool-contract.prevents: Conventions written for one tool while the team runs six. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md and not AGENTS.md; Cursor, Codex and Copilot read AGENTS.md and not CLAUDE.md, so a single-file project has documented its rules for a fraction of its agents.
crosstool-contract.enforcedBy: regeneration; a check that the pointer resolves
crosstool-contract.standard: AGENTS.md — read natively by around thirty agents

evidence.outcome: AGENTS.md plus an 82-token CLAUDE.md pointer: reach of ten agents from one text.

contract-budget.name: A token ceiling on what every agent reads
contract-budget.what: The always-on contract is held to a budget; detail moves into skills reached on demand.
contract-budget.prevents: A contract nobody follows because it does not fit. Every token in it is paid on every task by every agent, and a six-thousand-token contract crowds out the task.

evidence.outcome: AGENTS.md measures about 6299 tokens, paid on every task by every agent.

skills-not-prose.name: Knowledge as skills, reached on demand
skills-not-prose.what: Procedures an agent needs sometimes live in .claude/skills/ and are invoked when relevant, rather than sitting in the always-on contract.
skills-not-prose.prevents: A contract that grows until it is ignored. Contextual knowledge belongs where it is fetched on demand; only always-true guidance belongs in the contract.
skills-not-prose.standard: Claude Code skills, unified with slash commands

evidence.outcome: Five skills carry the procedures that would otherwise be five sections of the contract.

subagent-boundaries.name: Delegation boundaries as subagents
subagent-boundaries.what: Work with its own context and its own definition of done — a review, an audit, a scoped search — runs as a subagent rather than inline.
subagent-boundaries.prevents: One context holding a task and its review at once, where the reviewer has already agreed with the author by construction.

evidence.outcome: Two subagents own conformance review and promotion scouting, both of which need a context that is not the author's.

headless-agent.name: An agent that runs with nobody at the keyboard
headless-agent.what: The same settings, hooks and permissions driven from CI or a schedule, not only from an interactive session.
headless-agent.prevents: A factory that only produces while someone is watching it. Headless mode reuses the interactive configuration, so this costs a workflow file rather than a second setup.
headless-agent.enforcedBy: a workflow that runs the agent in one shot
headless-agent.standard: Claude Code headless mode; the same hooks and permissions apply

dependency-audit.name: The dependency audit in the gate, not in someone's memory
dependency-audit.what: The project's own package manager runs its audit as part of the gate, with the result read as distinct advisories rather than as dependency paths.
dependency-audit.prevents: A published vulnerability sitting in the tree for months because the audit is something a person remembers to run.

cost.ongoing: a decision per advisory, and most are transitive with no fix published

dependency-audit.enforcedBy: npm, pnpm or yarn audit in the gate graph
dependency-audit.standard: OpenSSF Scorecard treats a maintained dependency check as a baseline practice
dependency-audit.deliveredBy: a gate stage, once the gate exists — no file of its own

evidence-pack.name: The proof a reviewer reads instead of the diff
evidence-pack.what: One document per change: what changed, whether the gate and the project's own checks hold, what the measurements say, and what was not checked.
evidence-pack.prevents: The reviewer becoming the constraint. Everything upstream — the spec, the generator, the gate — moves faster than one person can absorb proof from a diff.

cost.ongoing: none; it is assembled from checks already running

evidence-pack.enforcedBy: ds evidence, which fails closed — a check that did not run is not one that passed
evidence-pack.standard: artifact-and-handoff models of delivery name this the bottleneck of the feature path
evidence-pack.deliveredBy: the `ds evidence` command, run per change — no file of its own
